hold_text: pr-landing R5 refuses self-landing on src/units/accounts/clients.py and src/web/api/routers/diag.py, Tier-2 BY PATH, and the guard is right. This is the instrument that settles whether trade 5471's protective legs were cancelled at its close or days earlier — the operator's stated primary task — so it needs a merge click. IT ALSO SUPERSEDES #11564: that branch is merged into this one, so merge THIS and close #11564, or #11564 will conflict on diag.py's import block.
why: READ-ONLY DIAGNOSTIC, and it answers the operator's actual question. Adds `account_bybit_raw_order_history` + `GET /api/diag/bybit_raw_order_history` — the RAW Bybit get_order_history records for one symbol and window. WHY IT IS NEEDED: the operator's primary ask is 'we need to understand and fix the no brackets'. trades.sl_order_id / tp_order_id show a leg WAS placed at entry for trade 5471 (those columns are written only on the Partial branch, from a before/after snapshot diff of the venue's legs), and /api/diag/bybit_open_orders shows what rests NOW. Between those two, NOTHING could ask what became of a leg that no longer rests: consumed at the close (the position was protected throughout) or cancelled days earlier (it ran naked on real money for four days). Those are OPPOSITE findings and the lane cannot proceed without distinguishing them. `cancel_type` is the load-bearing field — Bybit distinguishes a user cancel from a venue-side clear such as Partial legs being cleared when a position closes. WHY THE EXISTING ACCESSOR CANNOT: account_order_status normalises to {order_id, status, filled_qty, avg_price, exec_time}, dropping createdTime, updatedTime, cancelType, triggerPrice and stopOrderType — exactly the fields that answer when and why — and it is per-orderId, so it cannot surface a leg the journal never recorded. Same reduction pattern as the position and closed-PnL paths, one endpoint further along. IT INCLUDES #11564: claude/mi-221-fix-closed-pnl-route is merged into this branch, so both diag routes now bind their keyword-only window with functools.partial before the POSITIONAL-ONLY run_account_read hop (it forwards to loop.run_in_executor, which takes no kwargs), and there is exactly one `import functools`. Kept together deliberately: shipping them apart would conflict on the import block. It also fixes a truncated backlog id in #11564's own comment, which would have failed check_backlog_refs on that PR — and then a line-wrapped version of the same id, which the guard also correctly rejected because a wrapped id is not contiguous and tracks nobody. VALIDATION: 33 assertions across the three raw instruments (8 order-history + 7 closed-PnL + 18 positions), all executed and passing in-session via a monkeypatch shim because pytest is not installed here. Registered in docs/api-tier-policy.md (coverage headline 107 -> 108, computed not asserted) and docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md. Guards: PASS 68 with the remaining failures being missing sandbox tooling only — pytest x2 (No module named pytest) and lint-imports exit 127 (command not found) — neither attributable to this diff. SAFETY: no existing function's behaviour changes; account_open_positions, account_bybit_open_orders, _bybit_position_protection, _bybit_order_status_lookup, account_order_status and every protective sweep are byte-for-byte untouched. Routes are token-gated and read-only; they place no order and return no credential material. No order was placed, modified or cancelled on bybit_2 or any account; every venue call is a GET. DOCUMENT-INDEX.md untouched (no new doc file), so document_index.py --write was not run and remains prohibited.
